question: Why do about 99% of Austrians consent to organ donation, but only about 12% of Germans?
answer: Not because Austrians are kinder. In Austria everyone is a donor unless they opt out; in Germany you have to opt in. Most people stick with whatever is already ticked. Thaler and Sunstein call such defaults the most powerful nudge there is.
move: Whatever is already ticked is usually what most people end up choosing.
simply: If your plate already has broccoli on it, you'll probably eat some. If you have to go and fetch it, you probably won't.
why: Pension plans, privacy settings and subscriptions all run on defaults. Checking them is one of the highest-value five minutes you can spend.
source: Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein, Nudge, 2008
reference: Richard H. Thaler and Cass R. Sunstein, Nudge (Yale University Press, 2008), ch. 11
